session.context:
pqac-9857e34f: The excerpt describes a 2021 study that developed and tested a holistic e-learning success model using structural equation modeling (SEM) with survey data from 537 university students in Jordan. The abstract states that quality factors—such as instructor, technical system, support service, educational system, and course content quality—had direct positive effects on students’ satisfaction, perceived usefulness, and system use, while self-regulated learning had negative effects. However, the excerpt does not report any specific SEM path coefficients or p-values for external factors influencing perceived usefulness or students’ acceptance of e-learning.
From Ahmad Samed Al‐Adwan, Nour Awni Albelbisi, Omar Hujran, Waleed Mugahed Al-Rahmi, and Ali Alkhalifah. Developing a holistic success model for sustainable e-learning: a structural equation modeling approach. Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su13169453, doi:10.3390/su13169453.

pqac-0e6f76a1: The excerpt states that the study used structural equation modeling (SEM) on survey data from 1,875 Romanian university students who took online courses during COVID-19. Its main finding relevant to the question is qualitative: external factors did not influence perceived usefulness, and perceived ease of use did not influence behavioral intention to use new technologies. However, the excerpt does not provide the actual SEM path coefficients or p-values for these relationships. It only notes that the TAM variables were validated and that e-learning satisfaction was linked to academic success.
From Melinda Timea Fülöp, Teodora Odett Breaz, Dan Ioan Topor, Constantin Aurelian Ionescu, and Larisa-Loredana Dragolea. Challenges and perceptions of e-learning for educational sustainability in the “new normality era”. Frontiers in Psychology, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2023.1104633, doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2023.1104633.

pqac-1e4e6b99: The excerpt describes a study that developed and validated a UX-based e-learning acceptance framework using structural equation modeling (SEM) on 513 valid student responses. It reports which constructs significantly affected behavioral intention (students’ acceptance of the e-learning portal): satisfaction, perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, information quality, self-efficacy, social influence, and benefits. It also states that perceived ease of use significantly impacted perceived usefulness and pleasure, while appeal significantly impacted pleasure and satisfaction, and pleasure significantly impacted satisfaction. However, the excerpt does not provide the actual SEM path coefficients or p-values for these relationships.
From Baqar Ali Zardari, Zahid Hussain, Aijaz Ahmed Arain, Wajid Hussain Rizvi, and Muhammad Saleem Vighio. Development and validation of user experience-based e-learning acceptance model for sustainable higher education. Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su13116201, doi:10.3390/su13116201.

pqac-f1e7ec7c: The excerpt describes a study using path analysis and structural equation modeling (SEM) to test a model linking system quality (SYQ), service quality (SEQ), and quality of life (QoL) to perceived ease of use (PEU) and perceived usefulness (PU), which in turn affect behavioral intention to use (BIU) and actual use of an e-learning system (AUE). It states that PU and ease of use were positively influenced by SYQ, SEQ, and QoL, and that PEU and PU positively influenced students’ BIU and AUE. However, the excerpt does not provide the specific SEM path coefficients or p-values.
From Mohammed Ayid Alqahtani, Mahdi M. Alamri, Amer Mutrik Sayaf, and Waleed Mugahed Al-Rahmi. Investigating students' perceptions of online learning use as a digital tool for educational sustainability during the covid-19 pandemic. Frontiers in Psychology, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2022.886272, doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2022.886272.

pqac-942786bd: The excerpt describes a study using SEM-PLS with an expanded TAM to examine students’ e-learning adoption during COVID-19. It reports that external factors such as experience (EXP), technology anxiety (TEA), and facilitating conditions (FC), along with students’ engagement (SEN), positively affected task-technology fit (TTF) and perceived ease of use (PEOU), which in turn influenced behavioral intention and adoption of e-learning for educational sustainability. However, the excerpt does not provide the specific SEM path coefficients or p-values for external factors influencing perceived usefulness or students’ acceptance.
From Omar A. Alismaiel. Using structural equation modeling to assess online learning systems’ educational sustainability for university students. Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su132413565, doi:10.3390/su132413565.

contexts.context: The excerpt is from a 2023 Heliyon paper on e-learning adoption for sustainable higher education in Sri Lanka. It describes a study using Theory of Planned Behaviour and Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) on 357 academics from public universities. The abstract reports that attitude and perceived behavioural control influenced e-learning usage, while subjective norm did not; behavioural intention mediated some relationships, and e-learning usage mediated the link to sustainability in teaching. It also notes moderation by gender, academic position, and computer literacy. However, the excerpt does not mention external factors, perceived usefulness, students’ acceptance, SEM path coefficients, or p-values for those relationships.
